summary: ```markdown # How to Make a Folded Pocket in Marvelous Designer ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to create a foldable pocket in Marvelous Designer. This guide will cover the step-by-step process to ensure clarity and ease of understanding. ## Selecting the Pocket Version First of all, we will use the basic pocket version. I have changed its color to pink to make it easier for you to identify this pocket version. ## Drawing the Middle Line 1. Select the line on both sides of the pocket. 2. Press the Shift key to select more lines. 3. Right-click and select the line that is created according to the curve. 4. Draw a middle line, which will be our starting point for folding later. 5. Right-click on this line and select Cut. Note that the middle line will not automatically form a line, which is what we want. At this stage, the pocket is divided into the left half and the right half. ## Deleting and Reactivating Lines - Delete the bottom line first, or reactivate it by right-clicking when selecting these lines and choosing the reactivate line panel. - Once the line is reactivated, it will no longer work, allowing us to pull these two panels apart. ## Preparing for Folding Before we start making the pocket fold, we need to harden the panel first. This will make it resemble a piece of paper, allowing us to easily apply folding functions later. ### Folding the Panel 1. Decide whether the panel folds outward or inward. In this example, we will fold inward. 2. Click on the panel in the 3D window and adjust the inner line according to the blue index point, which is where we will fold in later. 3. Copy this panel using the adjustment panel tool to select the entire panel, then copy and paste. 4. Arrange it in the 2D window and cut off the excess line, maintaining only the right side for folding. ## Moving and Hiding the Panel 1. Move the newly arranged panel in the 3D window and hide it behind the original panel. 2. Next, we will prepare the box. ### Adjusting the Inner Layer 1. The main panel on the outer layer must face the front, while the panel that is folded back should face the back. 2. Once the sides are aligned, turn the panel horizontally and move it to the inner side of the original panel. 3. Use the adjustment panel tool to sew the sides together. ## Setting the Folding Angle If you are unsure where to sew, you can use the support point in the 3D window for guidance. ### Folding Angle Adjustment - After sewing the panel, notice that it automatically turns over because we did not set the folding angle for the panel line. - The folding angle of the model is 180 degrees, which is equal to flat. Set its folding angle to 0 for proper folding. This process is similar to the one we used for making the workbook pocket. Make sure that the two panels are facing each other when setting the folding angle. ## Copying and Adjusting Panel Lines 1. Select the panel line connected to the panel, use Ctrl C and Ctrl R to create a new panel line close to the existing one. 2. Since our panel line has been folded inward, we still need to compensate for the part that is folded outward. 3. Turn the panel line over in the storage space and position it correctly relative to the printed panel line. ### Creating New Panel Lines 1. Create a new panel line using the auxiliary point in the 3D window and don't forget to set its folding angle. 2. This time, since we are facing each other, set the folding angle to 360 degrees for inward folding. ## Final Adjustments and Merging 1. Select the part of the folding that was just created, use Ctrl C, Ctrl R to copy it to the other side. 2. Use the line powder tool (shortcut key N) to merge the two sides together. 3. Pay attention to the newly created panel line, which does not have a set folding angle. Switch to the edit panel line tool to adjust it to 0 degrees for proper folding. ## Completing the Pocket 1. Now, sew the middle section. 2. Check the folding angle applied in the middle. If it’s flat, no adjustment is needed. 3. To merge, use the edge panel line tool. Select the panel line and click Merge. **Note:** Be cautious, as merging can cause some deformation in the grid due to the particle diameter being large and the number of grids being small. ### Inner Line Creation Create a new inner line and apply the folding angle to it after merging. ## Repeating Operations Repeat the previous operations for the right side panel line. After merging, apply the folding angle accordingly. ### Drawing Panel Lines Again After merging, draw the panel lines again for future adjustments. ## Final Sewing and Simulation 1. Use the free sewing tool to sew the point to both sides. 2. Switch to the edge sewing tool to adjust the sewing line as needed. 3. Open the simulation by pressing the control key and ensure that the sewing lines are properly aligned. ## Conclusion In this tutorial, we covered how to create a foldable pocket in Marvelous Designer, including selecting the pocket version, adjusting lines, folding techniques, sewing, and merging. By following these steps, you will be able to create a well-structured foldable pocket for your designs. ```
